verdict.rationale: Lago documents event ingestion through a POST /api/v1/events endpoint, and its own docs state it deduplicates events so a duplicate is billed once, which covers idempotent ingestion. Nothing in the pack shows backdated or historical timestamps, or any high-volume or streaming throughput, so only about half the story is evidenced. Missing for 10: backdating/timestamp support for late events, evidence of high-volume streaming ingestion (batch endpoints, throughput limits), explicit token/compute-second metering examples, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can stream high-volume usage events — API calls, tokens, compute-seconds — into a metering pipeline with idempotent ingestion and backdating support

citations.quote: Lago uses it for deduplication: if the same event arrives twice, it is billed once.
Lago turns usage into invoices. You send events describing what your customers consumed
